# Plan benchmark corpus

Nine 256×192 PNGs (about 0.55 MB in all) that the plan benchmark and its tests read.

## Provenance and license

**Every image here is generated by code in this repository** (`paint.ts`, `scenes.ts`, `generate.ts`). None is a photograph, none is downloaded or derived from anyone else's work, and there is nothing third-party to attribute. They are released under the same terms as the rest of the repository.

Regenerate byte for byte with:

```bash
npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts lib/paint/plan/fixtures/generate.ts
```

| file | what it stands in for |
|---|---|
| `portrait-light.png` | light skin, dark jacket, neutral wall (portrait / skin) |
| `portrait-deep.png` | deep skin, pale jacket, warm wall (portrait / skin, high value contrast) |
| `landscape.png` | sky with clouds, hills, meadow, dark foliage, a path |
| `interior-warm.png` | lamp-lit room with a cool window, wood floor, red sofa |
| `high-key.png` | white porcelain on white, pale shadows, nearly all light values |
| `low-key.png` | apple and pear emerging from near-black, nearly all dark values |
| `still-life-muted.png` | grey-beige-olive jug, bottle and bowl; very low chroma |
| `sunset.png` | saturated violet, magenta and orange sky over a silhouette |
| `fruit-saturated.png` | red, yellow, orange and green fruit on a teal cloth; high chroma |

## What this corpus can and cannot show

These are *stand-ins* for photos: smooth shading, soft edges, some texture and about one level of sensor noise. They cover the color regimes a painter meets, but they are cleaner and simpler than real pictures (no fine texture, few distinct hues per scene, no JPEG or lens artifacts). Numbers measured on them compare algorithms against each other on this mix of colors. They do not tell you how a plan looks on your own photo.

## Adding real photos

Drop 8-bit, non-interlaced PNGs into this folder (resize to about 256 px wide so the repo stays light):

```bash
sips -Z 256 -s format png ~/Pictures/thing.jpg --out lib/paint/plan/fixtures/thing.png
```

Anything you add is picked up automatically and reported as a separate `photo` group by `npm run benchmark:plan`. The ratchets in `plan.test.ts` only read the generated images, so adding photos never breaks them. Only commit photos you have the right to publish, and record their source and license in this file.
